question: In a three-dimensional coordinate model, two fixed points are marked as $P(2,-1,4)$ and $Q(8,5,-2)$. A point $M$ is placed at the midpoint of $PQ$. Another point $R$ is placed on the segment $MQ$ so that $MR\:RQ=2:1$. The students use position vectors and the section formula to locate the two new points and then compare the component vectors along the original segment $PQ$.(a) Write the position vectors of $P$ and $Q$.(b) Determine the position vector of the midpoint $M$.(c) Find the position vector of $R$.(d) Use the components of $\overrightarrow{PR}$ and $\overrightarrow{RQ}$ to determine the ratio $PR\:RQ$.
explanation: (a)The position vectors are`\vec{p}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}`and`\vec{q}=8\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-2\hat{k}`(b)The midpoint position vector is`\vec{m}=\frac{\vec{p}+\vec{q}}{2}\vec{m}=\frac{(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k})+(8\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-2\hat{k})}{2}\vec{m}=5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}`(c)Since $R$ divides $MQ$ internally in the ratio $2:1$,`\vec{r}=\frac{2\vec{q}+\vec{m}}{3}\vec{r}=\frac{2(8\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-2\hat{k})+(5\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})}{3}\vec{r}=7\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{k}`(d)`\overrightarrow{PR}=\vec{r}-\vec{p}=5\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-5\hat{k}`Also,`\overrightarrow{RQ}=\vec{q}-\vec{r}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}`Thus,`\overrightarrow{PR}=5\overrightarrow{RQ}`Therefore,`PR:RQ=5:1`
